claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A machine-learning interatomic-potential approach combined with ab initio calculations can separately predict lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach will reduce mean absolute error by 15% relative to existing analytical approaches.
The approach is intended to combine machine-learning interatomic-potential simulations with ab initio calculations.
The prediction is intended to apply below 200 K.
The prediction is intended to apply from 300 to 1200 K.
The approach is intended to apply to defective or impure samples, including material containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Defects and impurities are relevant components of the alloy's atomic-scale complexity.
Capturing atomic-scale complexity with machine-learning interatomic potentials enables separate prediction of lattice and electronic heat transport.
The proposed approach will predict heat transport more accurately than existing analytical approaches.
The proposed approach will achieve a mean absolute error of no more than 2.5 W/(K m).
Existing analytical baselines include approaches coupling DFT-derived elastic properties to analytical conductivity estimates.
Oxygen and other impurities may affect prediction accuracy.
The proposed machine-learning interatomic potential may fail to capture some relevant atomic-scale complexity.
The test will compare predictions with measurements on HfNbTaTiZr samples having varying defect and impurity levels.
An MAE greater than 5 W/(K m) will falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of the predicted lattice and electronic contributions to match measurements within 10% will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires MAE at or below 2.5 W/(K m), whereas the hypothesis is declared falsified only above 5 W/(K m). Results between 2.5 and 5 W/(K m) would violate the prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
